subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A term newborn boy develops hypotonia, poor feeding, and tachypnea on the second day of life. He has a pungent odor described as sweaty feet, and abdominal ultrasound shows enlarged, echogenic kidneys. Laboratory studies show glucose 35 mg/dL, a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, mild hyperammonemia, and normal lactate. Urine organic acid analysis shows glutaric, ethylmalonic, adipic, and suberic acids, and plasma acylcarnitines show elevations of multiple chain lengths from C4 to C18.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric acidemia type II)

explanation_correct: Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric acidemia type II) results from defects in electron transfer flavoprotein or its dehydrogenase, which are shared by many acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. Hence fatty acid oxidation and branched-chain amino acid oxidation are both impaired, giving a broad-chain acylcarnitine profile, dicarboxylic aciduria, nonketotic hypoglycemia, and congenital anomalies such as renal cystic dysplasia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency elevates only medium-chain acylcarnitines such as C8 and does not cause congenital renal anomalies or a broad C4 to C18 pattern.
explanation_incorrect.C: Propionic acidemia causes ketotic hyperammonemia with elevated propionic acid and propionylcarnitine (C3), not a broad-chain acylcarnitine pattern.
explanation_incorrect.D: Systemic primary carnitine deficiency causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia and cardiomyopathy without dicarboxylic aciduria, multiple acylcarnitine elevations, or cystic kidneys.
explanation_incorrect.E: Isovaleric acidemia elevates isovalerylglycine and C5 acylcarnitine and produces a sweaty-feet odor, but not multisystem dicarboxylic aciduria or renal anomalies.

educationalObjective: A neonate with nonketotic hypoglycemia, sweaty-feet odor, cystic kidneys, and a broad-chain acylcarnitine plus dicarboxylic aciduria pattern has multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric acidemia type II).
